title: Control engineering changes and recover prior states
statement: Project decision owners, engineers, and maintainers need to evolve coherent engineering states through controlled changes while preserving the ability to identify, compare, and recover retained prior states, resume recorded work, and restore retained operational history from a valid backup with its original decisions and provenance.

what.problem: Changes can obscure earlier engineering states and their provenance, while interruptions can separate unfinished work from its context and decision authority. When operational records are local and separate from the engineering definition, loss of the only local copy can also erase work history even though the current model remains available.
what.desired_outcome: Participants can identify and compare retained states, continue controlled work with its recorded context and authority, and restore or transfer retained operational records and evidence from an identifiable valid backup without changing their original meaning.

why.rationale: A current model alone cannot explain how it came to exist, establish what an earlier assessment examined, or support reliable recovery of a previous engineering state. Controlled work also needs continuity after interruptions and respect for the project's decision authority. Keeping operational history outside the current engineering tree must not make continuity depend on one unprotected local copy.

stakeholders: Engineering agents acting within project authority

conditions: Applies when changes are proposed, assessed, adopted, corrected, or retired, and when a retained baseline is inspected or recovered. It also applies when in-progress work is interrupted, resumed, or handed to another participant.

Retain active work, unresolved findings, applicable decisions, and evidence needed for current reliance until resolved or coherently replaced. Retained baselines have no automatic age-based expiry; release of retained material is a separate controlled retention-policy decision that first resolves surviving dependencies.

Also applies when creating an operational backup, restoring after loss or interruption, transferring retained work to another local environment, or migrating its storage representation. Backup and transfer do not renew assessments or authorize engineering actions.

contexts: Across Changes, Baselines, configuration management, and provenance in the governed engineering environment.

The selected project operational store, retained evidence artifacts, and explicitly selected backup or restoration destination, initially for one local checkout and one user with one or more local agents.

how.approach: Identify coherent Baselines, control transitions, and preserve recoverable states and their provenance under the selected retention policy. In the initial authoring profile, a retained baseline identifies its governed requirement and asset definitions, relationship facts, applicable metamodel and rules, source provenance, and any realization or assurance material included in its declared scope. References alone do not claim recovery of unavailable external content. On-demand recovery selects an intact retained baseline and reproduces its recorded authoritative content and meaning; unavailable or incomplete recovery is reported explicitly. Keep current work context available for resumption and distinguish project decision authority from assessment results and suggested actions; SR-006 and SR-007 elaborate these obligations. Preserve an identifiable coherent backup of selected operational records and retained artifacts, with project association, interpretation information and integrity evidence. Restore or transfer only its declared scope and report unavailable, incomplete, incompatible or failed outcomes explicitly. Distinguish operational backup restoration from engineering Baseline recovery and interrupted transaction recovery. IR-001 retains ownership of current definitions and applicable rationale; IR-008 owns the supported command boundary.

how_much.scope: Covers Changes, Baselines, configuration management, revision provenance, and historical meaning under the project's retention policy. It does not require permanent working-tree copies, a particular version-control technology, or a specific external handoff service. Recovery applies to retained states. It also covers continuity of recorded in-progress work and human decision authority under the selected project policy, without requiring a new confirmation for every already-authorized action. Completed historical material may leave the current working view only after its original meaning is recoverable and current dependencies are reconciled. The refined scope includes recovery from an available intact retained Baseline and restoration of selected operational history and retained evidence from an available valid backup, including after loss of the original local operational store. It makes no elapsed recovery-time, recovery-point or automatic backup-frequency commitment. Unsaved work, changes after the selected backup, and destruction or unavailability of every usable retained copy remain outside a complete-recovery claim. Hosted backup, distributed synchronization and automatic merging of divergent histories are excluded. Current engineering definitions remain understandable without operational history; missing history must not be represented as an empty work history or successful assessment.
limits: Zero loss or alteration of the selected baseline's recorded authoritative content, identities, relationships, and provenance in a recovery declared complete. This bound is relative to that baseline, not to later unrecorded work.

A restoration declared complete preserves the selected backup scope, record and subject identities, relationships, original decisions, assessment meaning and required retained artifact content. This claim does not include later unrecorded or unbacked-up work.

assumptions: Engineering Baseline recovery requires an intact retained Baseline and applicable interpretation rules. Operational restoration requires an accessible valid backup containing the declared records and retained artifact scope; the original operational store need not survive.
The user or selected backup arrangement keeps a usable copy outside the failure scope against which recovery is expected; no hosted storage service is supplied by this requirement.
constraints: Backup, import and restoration preserve historical meaning and do not grant fresh approval, evidence applicability or action authority.
Retirement and migration must resolve current dependencies and preserve required originals; a new storage representation does not authorize deletion of the only usable evidence.

sources.basis: Controlled transitions, identifiable baselines, recoverable states, and historical integrity.
